idiom_name: opaque struct + one translation unit per concept (ADT module)
implementation_notes: C has no class, so the contour is hand-written: a header forward-declares the struct and declares the concept's operations, while the struct definition and the static helper functions live only in the concept's .c file; every operation takes the handle as its first argument and the concept's name as a prefix. The translation unit is what keeps internals in and the API out, so the boundary must be maintained by discipline - nothing in the language enforces it. If the concept genuinely spans several .c files, share the representation through a private header (name_private.h) rather than exposing it in the public one.
pitfalls: Nothing enforces the boundary: a leaked struct definition or a non-static helper in the public header lets clients manipulate the representation and re-scatters the concept.
Emulating member functions with per-instance function pointers wastes memory on every object and blocks inlining; prefixed free functions (string_*) are the idiomatic form.
A translation unit that needs 'and' to be described holds two concepts; splitting it is cheap, whereas un-splitting it later is not.
